source_text: Ideo et verbis illis, Ave gratia plena, primum Angelus ipsam salutando compellavit: Dominus tecum. Et non terrenus sponsus; sed ipse sanctificationis Dominus, pater castitatis, incorruptionis auctor, et libertatis dator; salutis procurator, et verae pacis conservator, atque largitor: qui ex terra virgine creavit hominem, et ex illius latere ac costa Evam assumpsit: Hic Dominus tecum, et rursum ex te.
thought_title: The Lord with Mary and not an earthly bridegroom
orientation: The preacher explains to his hearers what Gabriel meant when he said the Lord is with Mary.
pass_a_gloss: For this reason also with those words, Hail full of grace, first the angel addressed her by greeting her: The Lord with you. And not an earthly bridegroom; but the very Lord of sanctification, father of chastity, author of incorruption, and giver of freedom; manager of salvation, and preserver and bestower of true peace: who from virgin earth created man, and from his side and rib took Eve: This Lord with you, and again from you.

choices.why: Brief glossary fixes gratia plena as full of grace, and Ave is a greeting address
Announcement of present companionship in the greeting, not a wish or blessing
rejected: May the Lord be with you

choices.why: terrenus contrasts a human husband with the Lord named after, and sponsus means bridegroom
Keeps virgine applied to earth as in source, setting up the parallel with Mary

pass_b_english: For this reason too, Gabriel first greeted her and spoke to her with those words: "Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with you" (Luke 1:28). The one with you is no earthly bridegroom, but the Lord himself of sanctification, the Father of chastity, the Author of incorruption, and the Giver of freedom. He is the Steward of salvation, and the Keeper and Giver of true peace. He made man from virgin earth, and from his side and rib he took Eve. This Lord is with you, and he is also from you.
